chapter: Countess Johnson's band and the Kansas City scene
title: Countess Johnson's piano style
summary: Her style fell between Earl Hines and Basie, fast and effortless; she never sang.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: Well, I'm just interested in Countess Johnson because I've never heard anything about her. I mean, did she play the same sort of style of Mary Lou, or was she a different style piano player?
No, she was different. She was, I would say, she was nearer, she was between Earl Hines and Basie.
I'd say she was nearer to Earl Hines. But she was fast. And she said something, she didn't show any effort or anything.
No. See, we had Bill Nolan; he played drums and sang with us. She never sang.
